mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when the UNRATE increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past two months signals supply-side weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in the past month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the past month, it signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past three months signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA and GDPC1 growth is negative.
